title: Real Forms and Real Semisimple Lie Algebras

items.title: Complexification of a real lie algebra
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra g_0, its complexification is g_0 tensor_R C with the unique complex-bilinear bracket extending the original bracket.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.title: Complexification has a canonical conjugation with fixed algebra g zero
items.statement: The complexification has the conjugate-linear involutive Lie automorphism sigma(X tensor z)=X tensor conjugate(z), and its fixed algebra is canonically g_0.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: Check conjugate linearity, involutivity and bracket preservation on pure tensors. Write every tensor uniquely as X+iY with X,Y in g_0; sigma(X+iY)=X-iY, so the fixed points are exactly Y=0.

items.title: Real form of a complex lie algebra
items.statement: A real form of a finite-dimensional complex Lie algebra g is a real Lie subalgebra g_0 for which the complex-linear extension g_0 tensor_R C to g is an isomorphism.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.title: Real forms correspond to conjugate linear involutions
items.statement: Real forms of g correspond to conjugate-linear involutive Lie automorphisms of g; conjugate real forms correspond to conjugate involutions.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: A real form transports canonical conjugation to g. Conversely, for sigma define g_0=g^sigma and decompose every Z as (Z+sigma Z)/2+i(Z-sigma Z)/(2i); both summands are fixed and unique. These constructions are inverse, and applying a complex automorphism conjugates both the fixed algebra and involution.

items.title: Complexification preserves semisimplicity
items.statement: A finite-dimensional real Lie algebra is semisimple if and only if its complexification is semisimple.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: The complexified adjoint matrices show B_{g_C} is the complex-bilinear extension of B_{g_0}. A real bilinear form is nondegenerate exactly when its complexification is, so Cartan’s criterion in characteristic zero gives both implications.

items.title: Chevalley basis and real structure constants
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex
semisimple Lie algebra, let $\mathfrak h\subseteq\mathfrak g$ be a Cartan
subalgebra with root system $\Phi=\Phi(\mathfrak g,\mathfrak h)$
([[def-root-and-root-space-relative-to-a-cartan-subalgebra]]) and let $B$ be
the Killing form ([[def-killing-form-of-a-finite-dimensional-lie-algebra]]).
For a root $\alpha$ let $H_\alpha\in\mathfrak h$ be its Killing-dual vector
([[def-killing-dual-vector-of-a-root]]) and $h_\alpha=2H_\alpha/\alpha(H_\alpha)$
its coroot, so that $\alpha(h_\alpha)=2$
([[def-coroot-of-a-lie-algebra-root]]), and let
$(\lambda,\mu):=B(H_\lambda,H_\mu)$ be the inner product on
$E=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\Phi$ of
[[prop-the-roots-form-a-reduced-crystallographic-euclidean-root-system]].
Finally let nonzero vectors $e_\alpha^0\in\mathfrak g_\alpha$ be given for all
$\alpha\in\Phi$. Then there are nonzero complex numbers $c_\alpha$ such that
the rescaled vectors $e_\alpha:=c_\alpha e_\alpha^0$ have the following
properties, where $N_{\alpha\beta}\in\mathbb C$ is defined by
$[e_\alpha,e_\beta]=N_{\alpha\beta}e_{\alpha+\beta}$ when
$\alpha+\beta\in\Phi$, and $N_{\alpha\beta}:=0$ when
$\alpha+\beta\notin\Phi\cup\{0\}$; the pair $\beta=-\alpha$, for which
$[e_\alpha,e_{-\alpha}]=h_\alpha$ is not a multiple of a root vector, is
excluded from these definitions:

(i) $[e_\alpha,e_{-\alpha}]=h_\alpha$ for every $\alpha\in\Phi$;
(ii) $N_{\alpha\beta}=-N_{-\alpha,-\beta}$ for all $\alpha,\beta\in\Phi$ with
$\alpha+\beta\ne0$;
(iii) if $\alpha,\beta,\alpha+\beta\in\Phi$ and $\beta+n\alpha$ with
$-p\le n\le q$ is the $\alpha$-string through $\beta$, then
$N_{\alpha\beta}=\pm(p+1)$; in particular every structure constant
$N_{\alpha\beta}$ is an integer.

Moreover the real span
$$\mathfrak g_0:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{h_\alpha,e_\alpha:\alpha\in\Phi\}$$
is a real Lie subalgebra of $\mathfrak g$ regarded as a real Lie algebra, with
$\mathfrak g=\mathfrak g_0\oplus i\mathfrak g_0$; with respect to the basis
$\{h_{\alpha_1},\dots,h_{\alpha_r}\}\cup\{e_\alpha:\alpha\in\Phi\}$ determined
by a base $\Delta=\{\alpha_1,\dots,\alpha_r\}$ of $\Phi$, all structure
constants of $\mathfrak g_0$ are integers, and $\mathfrak g_0$ is a split real
form of $\mathfrak g$ ([[def-real-form-of-a-complex-lie-algebra]],
[[def-split-real-form]]). Finally, if
$\lambda_\alpha=\bigl((\alpha,\alpha)/2\bigr)^{1/2}>0$ and
$X_\alpha:=\lambda_\alpha e_\alpha$ for all $\alpha$, then
$[X_\alpha,X_{-\alpha}]=H_\alpha$ and $B(X_\alpha,X_{-\alpha})=1$ for every
$\alpha$, and the constants $C_{\alpha\beta}$, defined by
$[X_\alpha,X_\beta]=C_{\alpha\beta}X_{\alpha+\beta}$ for
$\alpha+\beta\in\Phi$ and $C_{\alpha\beta}:=0$ for
$\alpha+\beta\notin\Phi\cup\{0\}$, are real and satisfy
$C_{\alpha\beta}=-C_{-\alpha,-\beta}$ whenever $\alpha+\beta\ne0$.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
references.locator: Chapter VI, §1, Lemma 6.4 and Theorem 6.6, printed pp. 350-353, together with the split real form g_0 of (6.9) and Corollary 6.10 on printed p. 353; Chapter II, Lemma 2.18 and Corollary 2.37

references.title: Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras, Lectures 39-40
references.locator: Lecture 39, §39.1 (automorphisms of semisimple Lie algebras, Prop. 39.3) and §39.4 (the Cartan involution omega with omega(h_j) = -h_j, omega(e_j) = -f_j, omega(f_j) = -e_j, and the resulting real forms), printed pp. 180-184

items.title: Compact real form of a complex semisimple lie algebra
items.statement: A compact real form of a complex semisimple Lie algebra is a real form on which the Killing form is negative definite.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.title: Existence of a compact real form
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra has a compact real form.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: Choose a Cartan, positive roots and normalized Chevalley vectors with real integral structure constants. The real span of iH_alpha, E_alpha-E_{-alpha}, and i(E_alpha+E_{-alpha}) is bracket closed and complexifies to g. Root-space orthogonality makes the Killing form a direct sum of strictly negative blocks on these generators, proving compactness.

items.title: Conjugacy of compact real forms
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Any two compact real forms of a complex semisimple Lie algebra are conjugate by an inner automorphism.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: Let tau_1,tau_2 be their conjugations. Relative to the first compact form, tau_1 tau_2 is positive self-adjoint in the adjoint representation. Functional calculus gives its positive fourth root in the identity inner-automorphism group; conjugating tau_2 by it makes the involutions commute. Their simultaneous eigenspaces and the opposite Killing signs force equality, so undoing the conjugation gives the claim.

items.title: Split real form
items.statement: A real form g_0 of complex semisimple g is split when it contains a Cartan subalgebra h_0 for which every adjoint operator ad(H), H in h_0, is diagonalizable over R.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness up to isomorphism of the split real form
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every complex semisimple Lie algebra has a split real form, unique up to real Lie-algebra isomorphism.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: Use the real span of Chevalley generators and relations; the Cartan generators act with real root eigenvalues, so the form is split. Any split form admits a split Cartan and root vectors normalized to the same finite-type Serre presentation, which identifies it with the constructed form.

items.title: Cartan involution of a real semisimple lie algebra
items.statement: A Cartan involution of real semisimple g_0 is an involutive automorphism theta for which B_theta(X,Y)=-B(X,theta Y) is positive definite.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.title: Existence of a cartan involution
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every finite-dimensional real semisimple Lie algebra has a Cartan involution.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: Let sigma be conjugation for g_0 and choose a compact conjugation tau. Conjugate the compact form so sigma and tau commute. Then theta=sigma tau restricted to g_0 is real-linear and involutive; the simultaneous eigenspace decomposition is k_0 plus p_0, and the negative definiteness of B on the compact form gives positivity of -B(X,theta Y).

items.title: Conjugacy of cartan involutions
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Any two Cartan involutions of a real semisimple Lie algebra are conjugate by an inner automorphism.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: For theta_1,theta_2, use B_{theta_1} to polar-decompose their product as in Knapp Theorem 6.16. Its positive fourth root is exp(ad X) for X in the negative eigenspace, and conjugating theta_2 by this inner automorphism makes it equal theta_1; positivity rules out a residual nontrivial commuting factor.

items.title: Cartan decomposition of a real semisimple lie algebra
items.statement: For a Cartan involution theta, the Cartan decomposition is g_0=k_0 direct-sum p_0, the +1 and -1 eigenspaces of theta.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.title: Bracket relations and killing signs in a cartan decomposition
items.statement: In a Cartan decomposition, [k,k] is in k, [k,p] is in p, [p,p] is in k; B is negative definite on k, positive definite on p, and the two summands are B-orthogonal.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: Apply theta[X,Y]=[theta X,theta Y] to determine each bracket eigenspace. Since B_theta=-B on k and B_theta=B on p, positivity gives the signs; theta-invariance of B makes opposite eigenspaces orthogonal.

items.title: Global cartan decomposition for a connected finite center semisimple lie group
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let G be connected semisimple with finite center and a global Cartan involution theta, K=G^theta, and g_0=k_0 plus p_0. Then (k,X) maps to k exp X as a diffeomorphism K times p_0 onto G.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: Embed the adjoint group as a closed self-adjoint matrix group and apply polar decomposition: g=k exp X uniquely with X in p. Lift through G to obtain existence; the finite central kernel lies in K, so uniqueness survives. The differential is everywhere invertible by the positive-root formula for sinh(ad X)/ad X, and the explicit inverse from polar decomposition is smooth.

items.title: Riemannian symmetric pair of noncompact type
items.statement: A Riemannian symmetric pair of noncompact type is a Cartan pair (g_0,theta) with g_0 semisimple and no nonzero compact ideal; its global model is G/K.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.title: Cartan decomposition gives the invariant metric and curvature of g mod k
items.statement: For a noncompact symmetric pair, B_theta restricted to p defines the G-invariant metric on G/K, and at the origin R(X,Y)Z=-[[X,Y],Z]; hence sectional curvature is nonpositive.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: Ad(K)-invariance of B_theta makes the inner product descend from p=T_o(G/K). The Koszul formula for invariant fields and [p,p] subset k gives the displayed curvature. Invariance of B rewrites <R(X,Y)Y,X> as -||[X,Y]||^2, proving nonpositivity.

items.title: Cartan decomposition identifies p with the noncompact symmetric space
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Under the compatible global Cartan setup, X maps to exp(X)K as a diffeomorphism p_0 onto G/K.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: Factor the global diffeomorphism K times p to G through the right K quotient. Uniqueness of k exp X makes p to G/K bijective; local product charts and the smooth quotient map show it and its inverse are smooth.

items.title: Maximal compact subgroups exist and are conjugate in a connected finite center semisimple lie group
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. In the setup of global Cartan decomposition, K is maximal compact and every maximal compact subgroup is conjugate to K.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: K is compact because its adjoint image is closed in an orthogonal group and its central kernel is finite. The convex displacement function on p has a fixed-point minimum for every compact subgroup, conjugating it into K. Maximality gives equality, and conjugacy of Cartan involutions gives conjugacy of the resulting K’s.

items.title: Maximal split abelian subspace and real rank
items.statement: For a Cartan decomposition, a is a maximal abelian subspace of p and rank_R(g_0)=dim_R a. The later conjugacy theorem makes this independent of a; g_0 is split exactly when this equals its complex rank.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.title: Maximal abelian subspaces of p are conjugate by k
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Any two maximal abelian subspaces of p in a Cartan decomposition are conjugate by K.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: Choose regular H and H prime in the two subspaces. Compactness of K gives k minimizing ||Ad(k)H-H prime|| for the positive Cartan inner product. Differentiating along exp(tZ)k for every Z in k shows [Ad(k)H,H prime]=0. The p-centralizer of a regular element is its unique maximal abelian subspace, so Ad(k)a is contained in the second subspace; maximality and equal dimension give equality.

items.title: Restricted root and restricted root space
items.statement: For maximal abelian a in p, a restricted root is a nonzero real functional lambda with g_0^lambda={X:[H,X]=lambda(H)X for every H in a} nonzero; its multiplicity is dim_R g_0^lambda.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.title: Restricted root space decomposition
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. The adjoint action of a yields g_0=g_0^0 direct-sum over restricted roots g_0^lambda, with g_0^0=Z_{g_0}(a), finitely many roots, and finite real multiplicities.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: For H in a, ad H is self-adjoint for B_theta, so the commuting family ad(a) is simultaneously diagonalizable over R. The joint zero space is precisely the centralizer, the other joint eigencharacters are the restricted roots, and finite dimension gives finiteness and finite multiplicities.

items.title: Restricted root systems may be nonreduced
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Restricted roots need not be reduced: both lambda and 2lambda can occur; every irreducible finite nonreduced restricted-root system has type BC_r.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: In su(p,q) with p<q, diagonalize a in the standard p hyperbolic planes. Direct matrix commutators give roots ±e_i±e_j, ±e_i, and ±2e_i, so e_i and 2e_i both occur. For an irreducible nonreduced finite root system, take indivisible roots; root strings make them a reduced irreducible system, and the only possible added doubles occur in the short-root orbit. The rank-two string restrictions and the reduced classification leave exactly B_r with doubled short roots, namely BC_r.

items.title: Restricted weyl group
items.statement: For K and maximal abelian a in p, the restricted Weyl group is W(g_0,a)=N_K(a)/Z_K(a), acting faithfully on a and a*.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.title: Restricted weyl group is the reflection group of the restricted root system
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. The restricted Weyl group is generated by the orthogonal reflections in the restricted-root hyperplanes.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: For each restricted root choose X in g^lambda and use X+theta X, X-theta X and their bracket to build the rank-one compact subgroup; its normalizer element acts on a as s_lambda. These reflections lie in N_K(a). Conversely move any regular chamber back to the chosen one by them; an element preserving that chamber fixes a regular H, hence lies in Z_K(a). Thus the quotient is exactly the reflection group.

items.title: Positive restricted roots and nilpotent n algebra
items.statement: For a choice of positive restricted roots Sigma+, define n as the direct sum of g_0^lambda over lambda in Sigma+.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.title: Iwasawa decomposition on the lie algebra level
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For chosen positive restricted roots, g_0=k_0 direct-sum a direct-sum n as real vector spaces, and a plus n is solvable with n nilpotent.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: The root-space decomposition pairs g^lambda with g^{-lambda}; X decomposes into a k-part X+theta X and a positive-root part, while g^0=m plus a. This gives the direct sum. Brackets add restricted roots; positive height bounds make n nilpotent, and [a,n] subset n makes a semidirect n solvable.

items.title: Global iwasawa decomposition
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. In the global Cartan setup, with A=exp(a) and N the connected subgroup with Lie algebra n, multiplication K times A times N to G is a diffeomorphism.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: The Lie-algebra direct sum makes multiplication locally diffeomorphic everywhere. In the adjoint representation, A is positive diagonal and N unipotent; QR/Gram–Schmidt gives existence and uniqueness in the adjoint group. The finite central kernel is contained in K, so lifting gives a global bijection in G. Closedness of A,N and the explicit triangular inverse make the bijection a diffeomorphism.

items.title: Uniqueness and change of positive system in iwasawa decomposition
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. A and N depend on a and a positive system, but all choices are conjugate by K, with positive systems related by the restricted Weyl group.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: First conjugate maximal abelian subspaces by K. For fixed a, the reflection group acts simply transitively on restricted Weyl chambers, so a representative in N_K(a) carries one positive system and its sum n to the other. Exponentiation carries A,N accordingly.

items.title: Theta stable cartan subalgebra and compact split parts
items.statement: A theta-stable real Cartan subalgebra h_0 decomposes as t_0 direct-sum a_0 with t_0=h_0 intersect k_0 and a_0=h_0 intersect p_0, its compact and split parts.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.title: Every real cartan subalgebra is conjugate to a theta stable one
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every Cartan subalgebra of a real semisimple Lie algebra is conjugate by an inner automorphism to a theta-stable Cartan subalgebra.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: Complexify h_0 and choose compact conjugation commuting with its real conjugation. The induced Cartan involution stabilizes h_0. Conjugacy of Cartan involutions supplies an inner automorphism carrying that involution to the fixed theta; its image of h_0 is theta-stable.

items.title: Real cartan subalgebras need not be conjugate
items.statement: The compact and split Cartan subalgebras of sl_2(R) are not conjugate by any real inner automorphism.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: The split line R diag(1,-1) has ad with nonzero real eigenvalues, while the compact line R[[0,-1],[1,0]] has nonzero purely imaginary eigenvalues. Conjugation preserves the complex spectrum of ad, so the two lines cannot be conjugate.

items.title: Cayley transform of a theta stable cartan subalgebra
items.statement: For a theta-stable Cartan h and a real root or noncompact imaginary root alpha, choose a theta-compatible normalized sl_2 triple (E_alpha,F_alpha,H_alpha). The Cayley transform is the restriction to h of the inner automorphism exp((pi/4) ad(E_alpha-F_alpha)), with the standard factor i inserted in the noncompact-imaginary normalization; it replaces the corresponding split Cartan line by a compact line, or its inverse does the converse. Different compatible normalizations change the result only by the root centralizer used in the later conjugacy equivalence.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.title: Cayley transforms connect theta stable cartans in the classification
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Up to real inner conjugacy, theta-stable Cartan subalgebras are connected by finite sequences of real and noncompact-imaginary Cayley transforms; maximally compact representatives are mutually conjugate.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: If a theta-stable Cartan is not maximally compact, Knapp’s root criterion produces a real root whose Cayley transform raises compact dimension; iterate, which terminates by finite dimension. Reversing uses noncompact imaginary roots. At maximal compact dimension no such root remains, and the compact-part maximal-torus conjugacy argument gives one inner-conjugacy class.

items.title: Vogan diagram
items.statement: A Vogan diagram is the Dynkin diagram of the complexification with the involution induced by theta and painted fixed vertices marking noncompact imaginary simple roots, taken modulo diagram automorphisms and the standard reflection/painting equivalence moves.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.title: Vogan diagram of a real semisimple lie algebra is well defined up to equivalence
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. A maximally compact theta-stable Cartan and compatible positive roots give a Vogan diagram well defined up to the standard equivalence.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: Conjugacy of maximally compact Cartans accounts for inner diagram changes. Changing a compatible positive system is decomposed into simple reflections; the root sl_2 calculation gives exactly the prescribed painting toggle and adjacent-vertex changes. Diagram automorphisms account for relabeling. Reversing each step shows no additional identification is introduced.

items.title: Classification of real forms by vogan diagrams
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Equivalence classes of Vogan diagrams classify real forms of finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebras up to isomorphism.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: For a diagram, lift its involution to the pinned complex algebra and assign signs to fixed simple-root vectors from the painting; the Serre relations extend this to an involution theta commuting with compact conjugation, so sigma=tau theta is conjugate-linear and its fixed algebra is a real form. The constructed form recovers the diagram. Knapp Theorem 6.74 shows equivalent diagrams yield inner-isomorphic forms and that isomorphic forms give equivalent diagrams, establishing injectivity and surjectivity.

items.title: Satake diagram
items.statement: A Satake diagram uses a theta-stable maximally split Cartan and compatible simple roots: black vertices are compact imaginary roots restricting to zero on a, and arrows pair distinct white simple roots with the same nonzero restriction.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.title: Vogan and satake diagrams give equivalent real form classifications
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Vogan and Satake diagrams determine the same real-form isomorphism classes, though their decorations are not literally identical.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: Starting from the Vogan representative, perform Cayley transforms to a maximally split Cartan and restrict complex simple roots to a; zero restrictions become black and equal nonzero restrictions become arrow pairs. Reverse Cayley transforms reconstruct a maximally compact Cartan and its painting. The two operations commute with their equivalence moves and, because each reconstructs the same conjugation sigma, are inverse on real-form classes.

items.title: Complexification dichotomy for a real simple lie algebra
items.statement: If g_0 is a finite-dimensional real simple Lie algebra, its complexification is either complex simple or a direct sum s plus conjugate(s) of two isomorphic simple ideals interchanged by conjugation; the latter is a complex simple algebra viewed as real.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: Conjugation permutes the simple ideals of g_C. A proper conjugation-stable sum would have fixed points forming a nonzero proper real ideal, so the permutation is transitive. Because conjugation is an involution, every orbit has size at most two. In the two-ideal case projection identifies g_0 with one complex simple ideal regarded as real, and conjugation interchanges the factors.

items.title: Classification of real semisimple lie algebras
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every finite-dimensional real semisimple Lie algebra is a direct sum of real simple ideals, each either a complex simple algebra viewed as real or one of the compact, split, classical intermediate, or exceptional real forms in the Vogan/Satake list; this list is complete up to isomorphism.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: Decompose into real simple ideals. Apply the dichotomy to separate complex-as-real factors. For the remaining factors, their simple complexifications have classified Dynkin diagrams and the Vogan theorem gives exactly the finite equivalence classes of paintings/involutions; Borel–de Siebenthal reduction supplies one representative list and eliminates redundancy. Direct-sum uniqueness makes the resulting multiset classification complete.

items.title: Classical real forms of the classical complex lie algebras
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Up to the standard admissible ranges and low-rank coincidences, the classical real forms are sl_n(R), su(p,q), and su*(2m); so(p,q) and so*(2m); and sp_{2n}(R) and sp(p,q). The compact and split forms occur within this list at the appropriate signatures.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: Write the conjugations preserving real, Hermitian, quaternionic, symmetric, or skew forms and compute their fixed matrix algebras. Diagonalize the defining real/Hermitian/quaternionic forms to obtain the stated parameters. Compute the induced Vogan diagrams; the classification theorem proves exhaustion and identifies duplicates. Direct small-rank matrix isomorphisms account for A1=B1=C1, D2=A1+A1, D3=A3 and the other stated coincidences.

items.title: Representation theory of noncompact real reductive groups
items.statement: Harish–Chandra modules, (g,K)-modules, unitary duals, Plancherel theory, and Langlands classification require analytic machinery beyond this finite-dimensional real-structure block.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.title: A real form is merely the same complex lie algebra with scalars forgotten
items.statement: A real form is not merely a complex Lie algebra with scalars forgotten.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: Forgetting scalars doubles the real dimension, while a real form has real dimension equal to the complex dimension and is the fixed algebra of a conjugation.

items.title: All real forms of a complex semisimple lie algebra are isomorphic
items.statement: Real forms of one complex semisimple Lie algebra need not be isomorphic.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: For sl_2(C), su(2) has negative-definite Killing form while sl_2(R) has indefinite Killing form; an isomorphism preserves the form and its signature.

items.title: All cartan subalgebras of a real semisimple lie algebra are conjugate
items.statement: Cartan subalgebras of a real semisimple Lie algebra need not all be conjugate.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: Use the compact and split Cartan lines in sl_2(R); the cited proposition distinguishes their adjoint spectra.

items.title: Restricted root systems are always reduced
items.statement: Restricted root systems of real semisimple Lie algebras need not be reduced.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: The explicit su(p,q) calculation has both e_i and 2e_i, contradicting reducedness.

items.title: A plain dynkin diagram classifies real forms
items.statement: A plain complex Dynkin diagram does not classify real forms.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: The A1 diagram underlies both su(2) and sl_2(R); the missing compact/noncompact decoration distinguishes them.

items.title: Global cartan and iwasawa decompositions hold for every nonlinear cover without modified k
items.statement: The stated global Cartan and Iwasawa decompositions do not automatically hold on every nonlinear cover with the same compact K.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.

items.strategy: The universal covering group of SL_2(R) has infinite center; the inverse image of SO(2) is noncompact and must replace the compact circle. Thus the finite-center/K hypotheses cannot be erased.

title: Real Forms and Real Semisimple Lie Algebras — Examples

items.title: Compact and split real forms of sl two c
items.statement: The fixed algebras su(2) and sl_2(R) are respectively compact and split real forms of sl_2(C).

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: Display the two conjugations, verify their fixed matrices complexify to sl_2(C), compute B(X,Y)=4 tr(XY), and check negative definiteness on su(2) and a real diagonal Cartan in sl_2(R).

items.title: Cartan involution and k plus p for sl n r
items.statement: For sl_n(R), theta(X)=-X^T gives k=so(n) and p the symmetric trace-zero matrices.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: Check theta preserves brackets and squares to one. With B(X,Y)=2n tr(XY), -B(X,theta Y)=2n tr(XY^T) is positive definite; solving theta X=±X gives the two summands.

items.title: Polar cartan decomposition of sl n r
items.statement: The global Cartan decomposition of SL_n(R) is the polar factorization g=k exp X with k in SO(n) and X symmetric trace zero.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: Set P=(g^Tg)^{1/2}, X=log P and k=gP^{-1}. Then det P=1, X is symmetric trace zero and k is orthogonal with determinant one; uniqueness follows from the unique positive square root and logarithm.

items.title: Compact and split cartan subalgebras of sl two r
items.statement: The lines R[[0,-1],[1,0]] and R diag(1,-1) are compact and split theta-stable Cartan subalgebras of sl_2(R).

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: Compute their one-dimensional normalizers and their positions in k and p for theta=-transpose. Their adjoint eigenvalues are respectively imaginary and real.

items.title: Iwasawa decomposition of sl two r
items.statement: Every g in SL_2(R) has a unique KAN factor with K=SO(2), A={diag(a,a^{-1}):a>0}, and N={[[1,x],[0,1]]}.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: Apply Gram–Schmidt to the columns of g. The positive diagonal of the upper triangular factor is a,a^{-1}, and its unipotent remainder is N; positivity gives uniqueness.

items.title: Restricted roots of sl n r
items.statement: For sl_n(R) with diagonal trace-zero a, the restricted roots are e_i-e_j with one-dimensional spaces R E_ij.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: Compute [diag(h),E_ij]=(h_i-h_j)E_ij. Diagonal matrices form the zero space and the off-diagonal matrix units give all nonzero joint eigenspaces.

items.title: A nonreduced bc root system from a real form
items.statement: For su(p,q), p<q, a standard maximal split subspace has restricted roots of type BC_p.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: Use p hyperbolic two-planes and q-p residual negative directions. Block-matrix commutators yield ±e_i±e_j, ±e_i, and ±2e_i with the standard multiplicities, exactly BC_p.

items.title: Vogan diagrams for real forms of sl three c
items.statement: The real forms su(3), sl_3(R), and su(2,1) are distinguished by the Vogan data on A2.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: Compute the conjugations and Cartan involutions: the compact form has compact imaginary vertices, the split form uses the split involution class, and su(2,1) has one noncompact painted class. Standard Vogan moves identify alternate positive systems and leave these three classes.

items.title: Complex simple lie algebra viewed as a real simple algebra
items.statement: A complex simple Lie algebra s viewed as real is real simple and has complexification s plus conjugate(s), with conjugation interchanging factors.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: A real ideal complexifies to a conjugation-stable ideal of s plus s; projection shows it is zero or all. Map X tensor z to (zX,conjugate(z)X); this is a complex Lie isomorphism and canonical conjugation swaps the factors.

items.title: Two nonconjugate real cartan subalgebras
items.statement: sl_2(R) has two Cartan subalgebras that are not conjugate.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: Use the compact and split lines. Their ad spectra are {0,±2i} and {0,±2}; conjugation would preserve spectra.

items.title: Same complexification with different killing form signatures
items.statement: su(2) and sl_2(R) have the same complexification but different Killing-form signatures.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: The displayed bases give signatures (0,3) and (2,1), respectively, while both complexify to sl_2(C); signature invariance rules out a real isomorphism.

items.title: Hyperbolic space as so zero n one mod so n
items.statement: Real hyperbolic n-space is SO_0(n,1)/SO(n), with the Cartan metric of constant negative curvature.

references.title: Anthony W. Knapp, Lie Groups Beyond an Introduction, 2nd ed.
Pavel Etingof, Lie Groups and Lie Algebras

items.strategy: The identity component acts transitively on the upper hyperboloid and the stabilizer of (1,0,...,0) is SO(n). Identify p with boost matrices; the Killing-form metric is a positive multiple of the hyperboloid metric and the bracket curvature formula gives constant negative curvature after normalization.

items.title: The coadjoint representation, action and orbits
items.statement: Assume countable choice. For a finite-dimensional real Lie group G, the coadjoint action (g·alpha)(xi)=alpha(Ad_{g^{-1}}xi) is a smooth left action on the dual g*, and its orbits and stabilizers on g* are the coadjoint orbits and stabilizers; the fundamental field satisfies xi_{g*}(alpha)(eta)=alpha([xi,eta]).

references.title: Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry
Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry

items.title: Symplectic and hamiltonian lie group action
items.statement: Assume countable choice. A symplectic left G-action preserves omega. It is Hamiltonian when there is a coadjoint-equivariant map mu:M to g* such that d<mu,xi>=-i_{xi_M}omega for every xi, using xi_M=d/dt|0 exp(-t xi)·p.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4

items.title: Moment map and component hamiltonian
items.statement: Assume countable choice. An infinitesimal moment map is a linear covector-valued map mu:M to g* whose components mu^xi=<mu,xi> satisfy d mu^xi=-i_{xi_M}omega. It is an equivariant moment map when mu(gp)=g·mu(p) for the left coadjoint action (g·alpha)(xi)=alpha(Ad_{g^{-1}}xi); a Hamiltonian action has such an equivariant moment map.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4

items.title: Infinitesimal generator of a symplectic action is symplectic
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Every fundamental vector field of a symplectic action has zero Lie derivative on omega.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: The flow of xi_M is action by exp(-t xi), hence preserves omega. Differentiate its pullback at zero to obtain L_{xi_M}omega=0.

items.title: Moment map components generate the negative infinitesimal action
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Under the library convention, X_{mu^xi}=-xi_M.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: The moment identity gives i_{-xi_M}omega=d mu^xi. Uniqueness of the Hamiltonian vector field identifies X_{mu^xi} with -xi_M.

items.title: Equivariance is equivalent to the moment map poisson bracket identity
items.statement: Assume countable choice and connected G and M. A map satisfying the component moment equations is coadjoint equivariant exactly when {mu^xi,mu^eta}=mu^[xi,eta] for all xi,eta; for disconnected G the bracket identity is only infinitesimal equivariance and component-group equivariance must be added.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: Differentiate coadjoint equivariance along exp(-t eta), pair with xi, and use X_{mu^xi}=-xi_M to obtain the positive bracket identity. Conversely the identity says the derivative of mu(g·p)-g·mu(p) vanishes along every one-parameter subgroup; connectedness of G integrates this to equivariance. Connectedness of M turns locally constant component defects into constants.

items.title: Nonequivariance defect of an infinitesimal moment map is a constant lie algebra two cocycle
items.statement: Assume countable choice and connected M. If all component moment equations hold, c(xi,eta)={mu^xi,mu^eta}-mu^[xi,eta] is a constant alternating bilinear Lie-algebra two-cocycle with trivial coefficients.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: The antihomomorphism identity and the fundamental-field homomorphism show X_c=0, so dc=0 and connectedness makes c constant. Bilinearity and alternation follow from the bracket. Expanding Poisson Jacobi for three components gives dc_CE=0 with the trivial-module signs.

items.title: Moment maps for one action form an affine space over coadjoint fixed covectors
items.statement: Assume countable choice and connected M. Two equivariant moment maps for one action differ by a constant element of (g*)^G, and every such translation is again a moment map.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: Their xi-components have equal differentials, so connectedness gives a linear constant c(xi), hence c in g*. Subtract equivariance equations to get Ad*-invariance. Conversely an invariant constant changes neither component differentials nor equivariance.

items.title: Semisimple hamiltonian actions have unique equivariant moment map when one exists
items.statement: Assume countable choice. On connected M, an equivariant moment map for a semisimple Lie algebra is unique.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: An invariant covector annihilates [g,g]: infinitesimal invariance says c([xi,eta])=0. Semisimplicity gives [g,g]=g, so the translation space is zero.

items.title: Whitehead two removes the infinitesimal equivariance obstruction for semisimple actions
items.statement: Assume countable choice, connected G and M, and that every closed one-form -i_{xi_M}omega under consideration has a chosen Hamiltonian component linear in xi. If g is finite-dimensional real semisimple, constants can be added to make the infinitesimal moment map equivariant.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: Whitehead H^2(g,R)=0 writes c(xi,eta)=-b([xi,eta]) for a linear b after matching CE signs. Replace mu by mu+b; its differentials are unchanged and its new defect is zero. The bracket criterion and connectedness of G give group equivariance. This does not prove the component one-forms exact.

items.title: Noether conservation law for hamiltonian actions
items.statement: Assume countable choice. If H is G-invariant for a Hamiltonian action, then {mu^xi,H}=0 for every xi and mu is constant along the Hamiltonian flow of H.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: Differentiate H(exp(-t xi)·p) to get dH(xi_M)=0. With X_{mu^xi}=-xi_M and the Poisson convention this is {mu^xi,H}=0. Each component is therefore conserved; finite-dimensional duality makes mu itself constant along the flow.

items.title: Equivariant symplectomorphisms preserve moment maps up to a coadjoint fixed covector
items.statement: Assume countable choice and connected M. For an equivariant symplectomorphism phi of a Hamiltonian G-space, mu after phi minus mu is a coadjoint-fixed covector; literal preservation holds after a normalization eliminating that covector.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: Equivariance of phi identifies fundamental fields and symplecticity pulls the component equation for mu back to the same equation for mu∘phi. Thus both are equivariant moment maps for the same action; apply the affine-space proposition.

items.title: Cotangent lift is hamiltonian with tautological moment map
items.statement: Assume countable choice. For a lifted left action on T*Q, <mu(q,p),xi>=-p(xi_Q(q)) is an equivariant moment map under the library’s negative fundamental-field convention.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: Naturality makes the tautological form lambda invariant and lambda(xi_{T*Q})=p(xi_Q). Cartan’s formula with omega=-d lambda gives -i_{xi_{T*Q}}omega=d[-p(xi_Q)]. For g in G, substitute (g·p)(v)=p(dg^{-1}v) and xi_Q(gq)=dg((Ad_{g^{-1}}xi)_Q(q)); this proves coadjoint equivariance directly.

items.title: Tautological cotangent moment map is equivariant
items.statement: Assume countable choice. The tautological cotangent moment map is coadjoint equivariant.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: For the cotangent lift, (g·p)(v)=p(dg^{-1}v), and equivariance of fundamental fields gives xi_Q(gq)=dg((Ad_{g^{-1}}xi)_Q(q)). Substitute into -p(xi_Q) to obtain mu(g·(q,p))=Ad_g^*mu(q,p).

items.title: Kirillov kostant souriau form on a coadjoint orbit
items.statement: Assume countable choice. On a coadjoint orbit O, define omega_alpha(xi_O,eta_O)=alpha([xi,eta]) using the library’s fundamental-field convention.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4

items.title: Kks form is independent of lie algebra representatives
items.statement: Assume countable choice. The KKS formula depends only on the tangent vectors represented by xi and eta.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: If zeta represents zero, it lies in the stabilizer algebra, so ad_zeta^*alpha=0 and alpha([zeta,eta])=0 for every eta. Thus changing either representative leaves the value fixed; skew symmetry handles the second variable.

items.title: Coadjoint orbits are symplectic manifolds
items.statement: Assume countable choice. The KKS form is a smooth closed nondegenerate two-form on every coadjoint orbit.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: Homogeneous-space charts make the representative-independent form smooth and G-invariant. If omega_alpha(xi_O,eta_O)=0 for every eta, then ad_xi^*alpha=0, so xi is stabilizing and xi_O=0, proving nondegeneracy. Evaluate d omega on three fundamental fields; invariance reduces it to the cyclic sum alpha([[xi,eta],zeta]), which vanishes by Jacobi.

items.title: Coadjoint orbit inclusion is an equivariant moment map
items.statement: Assume countable choice. For the KKS form and standing signs, the inclusion O into g* is an equivariant moment map.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: Inclusion is coadjoint equivariant. For v=eta_O at alpha, d(mu^xi)(v)=eta_O(alpha(xi))=alpha([eta,xi])=-alpha([xi,eta])=-omega_alpha(xi_O,eta_O), which is the required component equation.

items.title: Product and opposite symplectic moment maps
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Product Hamiltonian actions have moment map mu_M+mu_N, and replacing omega by -omega replaces mu by -mu.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: Component differentials and contractions add on products, while both change sign for the opposite form. Equivariance is preserved by addition and negation.

items.title: Differential of the moment map and orbit orthogonal identity
items.statement: Assume countable choice. At p, ker dmu_p=(T_p(G·p))^omega and im dmu_p=ann(g_p).

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: The component identity gives <dmu_p(v),xi>=-omega_p(xi_M(p),v), proving the kernel equality. Its image is contained in ann(g_p); nondegeneracy gives rank dmu_p=dim T_p(G·p)=dim g-dim g_p, equal to dim ann(g_p), so containment is equality.

items.title: Regularity of a moment map is equivalent to local freeness
items.statement: Assume countable choice. dmu_p is surjective exactly when the infinitesimal stabilizer g_p is zero; hence a value is regular exactly when the action is locally free along its level.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: By the image formula, dmu_p is onto g* iff ann(g_p)=g*, iff g_p=0. A Lie stabilizer has zero Lie algebra exactly when it is discrete, which is local freeness.

items.title: Moment level is invariant under the coadjoint stabilizer
items.statement: Assume countable choice. G_alpha preserves mu^{-1}(alpha).

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: If mu(p)=alpha and g fixes alpha under coadjoint action, equivariance gives mu(gp)=g·alpha=alpha.

items.title: Characteristic kernel on a regular moment level
items.statement: Assume countable choice. If alpha is regular and i:mu^{-1}(alpha) to M, then ker(i*omega)_p=T_p(G_alpha·p).

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: Let W=ker dmu_p=(T_pGp)^omega. Its symplectic orthogonal is T_p(Gp), so ker omega|W=W intersect T_p(Gp). A fundamental vector xi_M lies in W exactly when ad_xi^*alpha=0 by differentiated equivariance, i.e. xi in g_alpha. Modulo the zero stabilizer algebra at a regular point, these are precisely T_p(G_alpha p).

items.title: Invariant horizontal form on a free proper quotient descends uniquely
items.statement: Assume countable choice. A differential form on a free proper G-manifold is the pullback of a unique quotient form exactly when it is G-invariant and horizontal.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: Use slice/principal-bundle charts to define the quotient form by evaluating on arbitrary lifts. Horizontality makes it independent of vertical changes and invariance makes it independent of the orbit representative. The local definitions agree and are smooth; surjective submersivity makes pullback injective, proving uniqueness.

items.title: Marsden weinstein meyer symplectic reduction
items.statement: Assume countable choice. If alpha is a regular value and G_alpha acts freely and properly on its level, M_alpha=mu^{-1}(alpha)/G_alpha has a unique symplectic form omega_alpha with pi*omega_alpha=i*omega.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: The regular-value and quotient theorems give the two smooth manifolds and a submersion pi. The restricted form is invariant and its contraction with every vertical fundamental field vanishes, so the descent lemma gives a unique closed quotient form. If a quotient tangent vector is in its kernel, lift it; the lift lies in the restricted radical, which the characteristic-kernel lemma says is vertical, so the quotient vector is zero.

items.title: Zero level symplectic reduction and dimension formula
items.statement: Assume countable choice. If zero is regular and G acts freely and properly on mu^{-1}(0), then M//G is symplectic and dim(M//G)=dim M-2 dim G.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: At zero the coadjoint stabilizer is all G. Regularity makes the level codimension dim G; quotienting the free G-action subtracts dim G again. Apply the reduction theorem for the form.

items.title: Dimension of a regular nonzero reduced space
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Under regular reduction at alpha, dim M_alpha=dim M-dim G-dim G_alpha.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: Surjectivity of dmu gives level dimension dim M-dim G. The free G_alpha quotient has fibre dimension dim G_alpha, yielding the formula.

items.title: Invariant hamiltonians descend to reduced hamiltonians
items.statement: Assume countable choice. A G-invariant Hamiltonian preserves every moment level and descends under regular reduction; its restricted flow projects to the Hamiltonian flow of the descended function.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: Noether gives preservation of the level. Invariance makes H|level descend to h. For every tangent lift v, pi* i_{X_h}omega_alpha=dh pulls back to dH(v)=omega(X_H,v); uniqueness modulo the vertical radical shows X_H and X_h are pi-related, hence their flows project.

items.title: Reduction commutes with products
items.statement: Assume countable choice. For product Hamiltonian actions and regular values satisfying the separate free proper hypotheses, reduction at (alpha,beta) is canonically the product M_alpha times N_beta with its product form.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: The product moment level is the product of the two levels and the stabilizer/action quotient is the product quotient. Pulling both candidate forms back gives i_M*omega_M+i_N*omega_N; uniqueness in reduction identifies them.

items.title: Reduction in stages for free proper regular actions
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Let H be a closed normal subgroup of G and let mu:M to g* be an equivariant moment map. Put mu_H=mu restricted to h. Assume zero is regular for mu_H and H acts freely and properly on its zero level. Then G/H acts Hamiltonian on M//H with residual moment map mu_bar([p])(xi+h)=mu(p)(xi). If zero is regular for mu_bar, G/H acts freely and properly there, and the one-stage G-reduction hypotheses hold, then (M//H)//(G/H) is canonically symplectomorphic to M//G.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: On mu_H^{-1}(0), mu(p) annihilates h, so the displayed residual covector is well defined; normality and equivariance make it independent of the H-orbit and G/H-equivariant. Pulling its components and the reduced form back verifies the residual moment equation. Its zero level is mu^{-1}(0)/H, so both final spaces are the same orbit quotient mu^{-1}(0)/G. Pullback of both final forms to mu^{-1}(0) equals the original restricted omega; uniqueness in reduction makes the canonical quotient diffeomorphism symplectic.

items.title: Shifting trick identifies reduction at alpha with zero reduction
items.statement: Assume countable choice. Under the regular free proper hypotheses, M_alpha is canonically symplectomorphic to the zero reduction of M times O_alpha with the opposite KKS form and diagonal moment map (m,beta) maps to mu(m)-beta.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: The zero set is {(m,beta):mu(m)=beta in O_alpha}, equivariantly identified with mu^{-1}(G·alpha). Every G-orbit meets the slice beta=alpha in one G_alpha-orbit, giving the quotient bijection. Inclusion of that slice pulls back the product form to omega; both reduced forms are characterized by this same pullback, so the bijection is symplectic. Regularity and freeness correspond by the stabilizer criterion.

items.title: Compact group symplectic actions admit an invariant compatible almost complex structure
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and countable choice. Every compact-group symplectic action admits a G-invariant omega-compatible almost-complex structure.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: Average a background metric over normalized Haar to obtain an invariant metric h. Define h(Au,v)=omega(u,v); polar decomposition J=A(-A^2)^{-1/2} is smooth, squares to -1 and is omega-compatible. Invariance of h and omega makes A, its positive square root, and J equivariant.

items.title: Compact group moment map can be averaged to an equivariant one when the affine obstruction vanishes
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice and countable choice. Let compact G act symplectically on connected M and suppose a linear infinitesimal moment map mu already exists. Then its constant affine non-equivariance cocycle is a coboundary: the Haar average mu_bar(p)=integral_G g^{-1}·mu(gp) dg is an equivariant moment map. This does not make nonexact component one-forms exact.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: Haar change of variables gives mu_bar(hp)=h·mu_bar(p). Differentiate each finite-dimensional component under the integral. Symplectic invariance transports d mu^{Ad_{g^{-1}}xi} to -i_{xi_M}omega, so the averaged component has the same required differential. Hence mu_bar is equivariant and differs from mu by a constant covector on connected M, explicitly trivializing the affine cocycle. Exactness was assumed when mu was supplied and is not produced by averaging.

items.title: Nonregular or nonfree symplectic quotients need not be manifolds
items.statement: Without regularity and a free proper action, a moment-map quotient can be an orbifold or a stratified symplectic space rather than a smooth manifold; singular reduction is deferred.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4

items.title: Convexity and toric classification for hamiltonian torus actions
items.statement: Moment-polytope convexity, Delzant classification, localization, and equivariant cohomology are later topics and are not asserted here as consequences of regular reduction.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4

items.title: Every symplectic action is hamiltonian
items.statement: A symplectic Lie-group action need not be Hamiltonian.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: Translation in one circle direction on the symplectic two-torus preserves dx wedge dy, but i_{partial_x}omega=dy is closed and has nonzero period, so no global Hamiltonian component exists.

items.title: An infinitesimal moment map is automatically equivariant
items.statement: Component Hamiltonians satisfying the differential equation need not form an equivariant moment map.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: On (R^2,dx wedge dy), translations have Hamiltonians y and -x; their Poisson bracket is a nonzero constant while the translation Lie algebra bracket is zero, giving a nonzero cocycle.

items.title: Moment maps are unique without normalization
items.statement: Moment maps need not be unique without normalization.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: For a circle action the coadjoint action is trivial, so adding any real constant to a moment map gives another one.

items.title: The cotangent lift moment map has a plus sign under the library fundamental field convention
items.statement: The cotangent-lift moment map does not have the formula +p(xi_Q) under the library convention.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: The proposition computes the component as -p(xi_Q); for translation of Q=R the plus sign has the opposite differential and generates the wrong fundamental field.

items.title: Every value of a moment map gives a smooth symplectic quotient
items.statement: Not every moment-map value gives a smooth symplectic quotient.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: For a weighted circle action on C^2, zero or a level containing points with finite stabilizer fails the regular/free hypotheses and the quotient has singular/orbifold points.

items.title: The general reduced dimension is dim m minus two dim g
items.statement: At a nonzero value the general reduced dimension need not be dim M minus twice dim G.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: The correct formula subtracts dim G and dim G_alpha. For a value with proper coadjoint stabilizer these differ from 2 dim G.

title: Moment Maps and Symplectic Reduction — Examples

items.title: Circle rotation on complex n space and its quadratic moment map
items.statement: Scalar circle rotation on C^n has a quadratic moment map with the sign fixed by the library convention.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: For exp(it) acting by scalar multiplication, the library generator is minus the usual rotation field. Contract it with sum dx_j wedge dy_j and integrate to obtain mu(z)=|z|^2/2 (up to a constant); differentiate to verify the sign and note circle equivariance is invariance.

items.title: Complex projective space as a circle symplectic reduction
items.statement: A nonzero scalar-circle level in C^n reduces to CP^{n-1} with a scaled Fubini–Study form.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: Choose the additive constant so the desired sphere is the zero level. The circle acts freely and the Hopf quotient is CP^{n-1}. The reduced pullback identity agrees with the standard Hopf definition of the Fubini–Study form; rescaling the radius rescales the form.

items.title: Weighted circle actions and weighted projective singular quotients
items.statement: Positive weighted circle actions yield weighted projective quotients and exhibit the failure of freeness when a weight exceeds one.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: For weights w_j, compute mu=(1/2)sum w_j|z_j|^2-c. On the level, a coordinate-axis point has stabilizer the w_j-th roots of unity; hence the quotient is weighted projective space and is generally an orbifold rather than the smooth quotient of the theorem.

items.title: Angular momentum as the moment map for rotations of a cotangent bundle
items.statement: The cotangent lift of rotations of R^3 has moment map equal to angular momentum after reconciling the negative fundamental-field convention.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: Identify so(3) with R^3 so xi_Q(q)=-xi cross q under the library convention. Then -p(xi_Q)=p·(xi cross q)=xi·(q cross p), so mu(q,p)=q cross p.

items.title: Cotangent reduction for a principal bundle at zero
items.statement: For a free proper action on Q, cotangent reduction at zero is canonically symplectomorphic to T*(Q/G).

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: The zero level consists of covectors annihilating orbit tangents. Such a covector is uniquely the pullback of a covector on Q/G, and quotienting by G gives a bundle diffeomorphism to T*(Q/G). Both tautological one-forms pull back to the same form, hence so do their -d derivatives.

items.title: Two sphere as a coadjoint orbit of so three
items.statement: Nonzero coadjoint orbits of SO(3) are spheres with KKS area form and inclusion moment map.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: Identify so(3)* with R^3 by the invariant dot product. The orbit of alpha is the sphere of radius r; using [xi,eta]=xi cross eta, the KKS value is alpha·(xi cross eta), which equals the standard area form divided by r (up to the fixed orientation). Inclusion is the cited moment map.

items.title: Grassmannians from unitary symplectic reduction
items.statement: A unitary matrix action on Hom(C^k,C^n) reduces at a positive central value to the Grassmannian Gr(k,n).

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: With omega=Im tr(dA* wedge dA), compute the U(k) moment map mu(A)=(i/2)(A*A-cI) in the chosen pairing. The level is the Stiefel manifold of scaled orthonormal k-frames, U(k) acts freely on frame changes, and the quotient sends a frame to its k-plane. The pullback identity defines the standard Grassmannian symplectic form.

items.title: Diagonal action and addition of angular momenta
items.statement: For a diagonal product action, total angular momentum is the sum of the factor moment maps.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: On a product of cotangent phase spaces, contractions split by factors, so d<mu,xi> is the sum of the angular-momentum component differentials. Thus mu=sum q_j cross p_j.

items.title: Shifting trick for a nonzero coadjoint orbit
items.statement: Reduction at a nonzero coadjoint value is realized as a zero reduction after adjoining the opposite orbit.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: Write the product moment map mu(m)-beta. Its zero set has beta=mu(m) in O_alpha; each G-orbit meets beta=alpha in exactly a G_alpha-orbit, and the restricted product form matches the original level form.

items.title: Reduced harmonic oscillator flow on projective space
items.statement: The scalar-invariant harmonic oscillator on C^n reduces to its projected Hamiltonian flow on projective space.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: The oscillator Hamiltonian is circle invariant and preserves the sphere level. Descend it through the Hopf quotient; the pullback calculation in the reduced-Hamiltonian proposition shows that its vector field is the projection of the oscillator field.

items.title: Irrational flow on a symplectic torus is symplectic but not hamiltonian
items.statement: An irrational constant flow on a symplectic two-torus is symplectic but not Hamiltonian.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: For X=a partial_x+b partial_y with irrational slope, L_X(dx wedge dy)=0. Its contraction a dy-b dx has a nonzero period when (a,b) is nonzero, so it is not exact and no Hamiltonian exists.

items.title: Zero angular momentum level with nonfree points is singular
items.statement: The zero angular-momentum quotient for rotations of T*R^3 contains nonfree strata and is not a smooth reduced manifold everywhere.

references.title: Ana Cannas da Silva, Lectures on Symplectic Geometry
Eckhard Meinrenken, Symplectic Geometry

source_locators: Lectures 21–24 and 26, especially Definition 22.1, Theorem 23.1 and its proof, Theorem 24.1, and §§24.3–24.4
items.strategy: The level q cross p=0 includes (0,0), fixed by all SO(3), and nonzero collinear pairs with circle stabilizer. Orbit dimensions jump, so the quotient dimension is not locally constant at the fixed orbit; the regular free theorem cannot apply.
